correctness.rationale: Facet equations are derived from the exact tetrahedral Gram matrix, and their strict support at all eight generators is checked algebraically for 1<lambda<3. At most one negative-orbit vertex can be illuminated by summing active-facet inequalities; four nonzero algebraically specified directions cover all eight. The sharp directional threshold follows from the necessary strict inequality (3s-1)T<0 for three illuminated positives and a matching explicit ray for s<1/3. Reciprocal affine symmetry treats lambda<1, and direct simplex/cube geometry treats lambda in (0,1/3] union {1} union [3,infinity). Exact rational facet and witness checks using the actual included verify.py corroborate the algebra; no finite enumeration is used as a continuum proof.

value.rationale: A fully natural deformation of the regular tetrahedron through its Catalan polar links an ordinary and fractional illumination collapse from 8 to 4 at a canonical cube endpoint, while a separate exact geometric breakpoint changes the maximum number of illuminated extreme vertices from four to three. All thresholds have exact proofs, the standard invariants have geometric motivation, and the result is a full family classification, not a random finite sample.
